vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-56854
vulnerability.description: golang.org/x/crypto/ssh: authentication bypass due to unenforced source-address restrictions

statements.impact_statement: The vulnerable code is the golang.org/x/crypto/ssh SSH SERVER path, which fails to enforce source-address restrictions declared in authorized_keys. The toolbox images run no SSH server. x/crypto reaches these images only as an indirect dependency of two scanner binaries, betterleaks 1.8.1 (x/crypto 0.53.0) and osv-scanner 2.5.1 (x/crypto 0.54.0), both of which are the latest upstream releases and neither of which yet builds against the 0.55.0 fix. Both run as short-lived CLI processes over a read-only source tree, neither listens on a socket, and betterleaks contains no reference to crypto/ssh at all (upstream code search: zero results). There is no reachable path from any toolbox entrypoint to ssh.ServerConfig. Deliberately NOT claimed for syft, which was upgraded to 1.51.1 because that release ships x/crypto 0.55.0 and genuinely fixes the issue, and which now scans clean without this exception: a fixable finding is fixed, not excepted.
statements.action_statement: Scoped to the exact affected x/crypto versions (0.52.0, 0.53.0, 0.54.0) so a tool that rebuilds against 0.55.0 or later stops matching and the gate re-arms by itself, with no edit here. Revisit when betterleaks or osv-scanner ship such a release, then drop the corresponding version and confirm the scan still passes without it. Re-evaluate immediately if any toolbox image ever gains a long-running or listening process.
